acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE DEADLOCK IS REAL AND WAS MEASURED, not argued: a claude-authored commit adding one rule to core/ failed the lane gate on four plugins/codex/lwb/vendor/ paths, because lwb_build.py vendors core into BOTH plugins and lwb_build --check fails if either drifts
plugins/*/lwb/vendor/ classifies as shared, so a core change is landable by a claude session while still requiring independent review

THE EXCEPTION IS EXACTLY vendor/ AND LEAKS NOWHERE: hooks/, bin/, skills/ and the plugin manifest under either lane still classify as that lane, including the near-misses bin/vendor_helper.py and plugins/codex/vendor/x.py
The deadlock test was confirmed RED against the pre-fix classifier by restoring it and re-running, and the leak test passes against BOTH versions, as a guard test should

HOLE CLOSED: a git-tracked file under vendor/ that the build does not produce is reported by name as a STOWAWAY and --check exits 1 -- a force-added .pyc ships in the plugin and is what the interpreter loads, while the reviewed .py never runs
HOLE CLOSED: a file replaced by a same-named directory is drift. dircmp files it under common_funny, which nothing checked, so _trees_equal returned True
The two hole fixes carry guards on the guards: identical trees still compare equal and an ordinary extra file is still drift, so the check was not broken into always-failing

unproven: PATH-TRAVERSAL IN THE WRITE HOOK, PLAUSIBLE AND PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED: the reviewer found 'plugins/codex/lwb/vendor/../bin/lwb_hook.py' classifies 'shared' and the write hook ALLOWS a claude Edit on it. It also found the identical shape already on main before this PR -- 'docs/../plugins/codex/lwb/bin/lwb_hook.py' was already shared+allow -- so this PR does not introduce it. CI is unaffected because the lane gate reads canonical paths from git diff-tree --name-only, and the write hook is the documented nudge, not the check of record. Normalising the path in _relativize would close it.

CASE VARIANTS ARE NOT EXEMPTED BUT ARE NOT LANE-CLASSIFIED EITHER: the reviewer measured 'plugins/Codex/lwb/Vendor/x.py' as 'other', which CI REJECTS because check_lanes errors on any class that is neither shared nor the agent's own. 'plugins/codex/lwb/Vendor/x.py' stays codex. Neither is a bypass, but the behaviour is incidental rather than designed.

SYMLINKS UNDER vendor/ WERE NOT REPRODUCED. The reviewer reasoned that git stores the link itself at its own path so the gate sees a shared path, and --check follows the link and compares content so the link must match build output. Reasoned, not tested.

THE STOWAWAY CHECK DEPENDS ON git ls-files. If git is unavailable or the directory is not a repo, it returns an empty list rather than inventing a pass or a fail -- covered by a test -- but in that state the check provides no protection at all and says nothing about it beyond the drift line.
